Duffett, Allum, Rice and Khlopin (who is not allowed to compete owing to his Russian nationality) travelled to Beaconsfield to run in the National Championship.
Apparently the success of Crichton, Dodkin and, lately, Khlopin, is causing him to look round for new blood, and he is once again casting envious eyes on the running ranks.
A pleasing feature of the race, from the Belgrave point of view, was the excellent walking of Paul Khlopin, which enabled him to finish 28th in the scratch race and 7th in the handicap.

Elson started off at a very fast pace, followed by Field and Saunders, with Khlopin close behind. Towards the end of the first lap Field was in the lead, but he suffered disqualification, and this again gave Elson the lead, closely followed by Saunders.
Saunders well deserves any success that comes his way, for he puts in some hard training, and it is he who was chiefly responsible for turning the third man, Paul Khlopin, into the fine walker he is.
